item.title: [10] Energy- and momentum-resolved Cooper-pair emission from a cuprate superconductor
item.description:
Last authors: Dirk K. Morr, Fahad Mahmood

Authors: Henry Amir, Jack Zwettler, Ka Ho Wong, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct hit: novel multi-electron photoemission (2e-ARPES) experiment on a superconducting material.

Tags: #ARPES #superconductivity #experiment

Abstract: Superconductivity arises from Cooper pairing, but conventional photoemission probes electrons individually rather than as pairs. Here we report the observation of Cooper-pair emission from an optimally doped cuprate superconductor using two-electron angle-resolved photoemission (2e-ARPES). Below the superconducting transition, we observe a distinct two-electron emission peak at zero pair binding energy and zero pair momentum that disappears in the normal state, revealing the characteristic fingerprint of a Cooper pair. Unexpectedly, the joint energy distribution broadens markedly along the relative-energy axis as temperature decreases, while the total energy width remains nearly unchanged. This anomalous behavior cannot be explained by instrumental resolution, static disorder or thermal broadening, and instead points to scattering processes involving collective excitations of the superconductor. Our results establish 2e-ARPES as a probe of both Cooper-pair emission and the many-body dynamics of the superconducting state.

item.title: [10] Magneto-ARPES as a direct probe of Berry Curvature and the Orbital Magnetic Moment
item.description:
Last authors: Bernd Braunecker, Luke C. Rhodes

Authors: Seohyun Kong, Bernd Braunecker, Luke C. Rhodes

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: ARPES

Tags: #ARPES #angle-resolvedphotoemission #photoemission #Berrycurvature #anomalousHall #monolayer #Halleffect #transport

Abstract: The Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment are central to the understanding of electronic transport phenomena such as the anomalous Hall effect, yet measuring these quantities directly with momentum resolution remains experimentally challenging. Here we show that angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements in a weak magnetic field (magneto-ARPES) provide a direct route to both quantities. We develop an analytic theory of photoemission in a weak magnetic field and show that, for any material, the first-order change in photoemission intensity is directly proportional to both the Berry curvature and the orbital magnetic moment, even in the presence of self-energy effects. For linearly polarised light, the matrix elements are unchanged to first order in the field, so the intensity change directly reflects these quantities. Using monolayer WSe$_2$ as an example, we show how both quantities can be extracted in a typical experiment. This finding thus points to magneto-ARPES as a general route for measuring the momentum-resolved Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment in quantum materials.

item.title: [9] Interaction-enhanced quantum to classical transport crossover temperature in a Luttinger liquid
item.description:
Last authors: Yen-Wen Lu, Michael Mulligan

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: title strong match: Luttinger liquid

Tags: #Luttinger #phonon #transport

Abstract: Strange metals are highly entangled gapless states of matter that exhibit anomalous transport, such as linear in temperature resistivity, over more than a decade of temperature. Why a single power law should be so robust is an open question. We propose a scenario in which interactions enhance the domain of certain scattering regimes, effectively suppressing other ``would-be regimes." We test this proposal in a one-dimensional Luttinger liquid coupled to a one-dimensional acoustic phonon. We use the memory matrix formalism to calculate the dc electrical and thermal conductivities at low and high temperatures, relative to the Debye cutoff on phonon frequencies, in both the ``clean" (umklapp scattering) and ``dirty" (disorder scattering) limits. We find the crossover temperature separating the low and high temperature regimes to be interaction-dependent, with repulsive interactions substantially increasing it, generally by more than an order of magnitude. This provides a concrete illustration for how interactions can extend a single transport regime over a wider temperature range.

item.title: [9] momipy: A time-resolved momentum microscopy data analysis workflow
item.description:
Last authors: Stefan Mathias (I. Physikalisches Institut, International Center for Advanced Studies of Energy Conversion)

Authors: Paul Werner (I. Physikalisches Institut, Georg-August-Universit\"at G\"ottingen, Germany), et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Tool for ARPES/momentum microscopy, directly relevant to the user's primary experimental expertise.

Tags: #method #ARPES #photoemission

Abstract: Photoemission momentum microscopy is an emerging approach to photoelectron spectroscopy that is transforming electronic band structure mapping at both laboratory-based and large-scale facilities. Its extension to time-resolved measurements has recently enabled major advances, ranging from the femtosecond imaging of exciton wavefunctions to dark-field photoelectron microscopy of light-induced dynamics and strong light-matter interactions. However, the rapid acquisition of high-dimensional data sets (including electron in-plane momenta $k_x$ and $k_y$, kinetic energy $E_\mathrm{kin}$, time $\Delta t$, and more) poses substantial challenges for data handling and analysis. A typical workflow encompasses data acquisition, exploratory visualization, calibration and targeted feature extraction, with data management ideally guided by FAIR principles. Here, we present momipy, a Python package that streamlines the momentum microscopy data analysis workflow efficiently and at low computational cost. Among other features, momipy provides interactive 4D data visualization, energy and momentum calibration, space-charge correction, and a broad selection of multidimensional data analysis routines, including binning, momentum-map extraction and time-, energy- and momentum-resolved model fitting. momipy is accompanied by a selection of interactive example scripts, supporting adoption of momipy by both experienced researchers and users new to momentum microscopy.
